newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Life wins vote for share conversion.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Life wins vote for share conversion.

text.p: Swiss Life/Rentensanstalt said holders of its participation certificates voted to convert their securities into shares as part of a management plan to turn the cooperatively-owned insurer into a listed company.
The company said 295,000 votes of 300,000 represented at an extraordinary meeting voted for the share conversion.
It said the meeting was attended by 449 investors holding 31.2 percent of all certificates.
Management plans to convert the certificates into shares by the end of August. The current certificates will make up eight percent of share capital.
Under the transformation plan, some 600,000 insurance clients who are now cooperative members will be asked to vote by mail between may 26 and June 20 on creating a public limited company.
If two-thirds of members approve, Swiss Life will register itself as a listed company on June 30.

After a transition phase with some conditional capital locked up in convertible bonds and loans, cooperative members will in the end hold 53 percent of share capital totalling 587.35 million Swiss francs or 11.7 million bearer shares with a face value of 50 Swiss francs each.
Today's participation certificate holders will have eight percent and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) 25 percent of share capital.
The remaining 14 percent will be in the form of convertible bonds.
